issuer: the police officer of the Islands, subject to the Island Council
note: Read 2026-10-30 in the Revised Laws of Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands (2017 revised edition, volume 1), on the Government of the Pitcairn Islands' site: the Local Government Regulations (Cap. 11), Part XI, Control of Traffic. The police officer issues a driving licence for a class of motor vehicle to a person over the age of 15 years who is fit and competent to drive (regulation 3, as amended 16 June 2004), so it is held from 15 (a learner's permit, also from over 15, for up to three months, isn't held). Regulation 4 (from 1 April 2004): a permanent resident's licence costs $25.00 and is valid for the rest of the holder's lifetime, which the form holds as no term in years (null); anyone else pays $10.00 for a licence valid to the next 31 March, which isn't held (the form's non-citizen fee is for a dearer one beside the citizen's). The dollars are the Islands' currency, New Zealand's. No identity card or exchange list is held. Held as lasting for life ("for the remainder of his or her lifetime") from 2026-10-30, when the form took it; until then its years were null, as if unknown (the lead).

sources.title: Revised Laws of Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands, 2017 Rev. Ed., Volume 1 (Local Government Regulations, Part XI)
sources.said: PART XI—CONTROL OF TRAFFIC ... shall apply to the police officer for a licence to drive such class of motor vehicle ... over the age of 15 years; ... in the case of every permanent resident of the Islands, upon payment of the sum of twenty-five dollars ($25.00), for the remainder of his or her lifetime; ... in the case of any other person, upon payment of the sum of ten dollars ($10.00), until the 31st day of March in the next following year;
